kanji_tips.tip: Write the kanji 10 times on paper. Muscle memory helps recall.
Study only 5–10 kanji per day. Small sets are easier to remember.
Say the reading out loud while looking at the kanji.
Create a small story for the kanji shape.
Link the kanji with a word you already know.
Review yesterday’s kanji before learning new ones.
Look for the radicals inside the kanji.
Write the kanji while saying its meaning.
Try to remember the kanji without looking after a few minutes.
Use the kanji in a simple word or sentence.
Imagine a picture that matches the kanji meaning.
Study a little every day instead of studying a lot at once.
Test yourself before checking the answer.
Group similar kanji together to notice the differences.
Practice writing from memory, not just copying.
